$comment: Retired vocabulary the DOR-855+ Language & IA program has moved off of, banned wave by wave (plans/language-ia-simplification.md). Adding a wave here is the ONLY change extending the gate needs — check-vocab-gate.ts and its allowlist mechanism stay put. A term is matched literally and case-insensitively, fenced with a word boundary at each end that HAS a word character: 'connection' does not fire on 'Connections', 'ConnectionState' or 'reconnecting', while a punctuation term like '...' matches wherever it appears in a copy position.

waves.note: "Connection" stops meaning network health in user copy — the word belongs to the Connections domain only (plan D2). Legitimate Connections-domain usage is allowlisted per file in allowlist.json, not exempted here.

"Mission control" and "cockpit" are retired for good — the operator ruled both out on 2026-08-24 and the category phrase became "one place" (meta/VOICE.md). This wave covers render-path strings in app source. The prose surfaces an AST walk cannot see — READMEs, docs MDX, blog posts, context7.json, the PWA manifest — are guarded by scripts/check-banned-words.sh instead. GitHub ships a product literally named "Mission Control", so a genuine reference to it is allowlisted per file rather than exempted here.

Typography, not vocabulary — but the same failure and the same fix. The app shipped 161 strings spelling an ellipsis "…" and 40 spelling it "...", and 88 apostrophes as `'` beside 72 as `’`, which render at different widths and read as two products. The house rule is one character each, written literally: `…`, `’`, `“`, `”` (contributing/design-system.md, "Punctuation"). `"` joined the ban after review found it live in production copy (`"{name}" will stop working…`, `MessagingConnections.tsx`) — it is the escape `react/no-unescaped-entities` actually pushes authors toward for a straight `"`, not `“`/`”`, which nobody in this codebase writes. A term here is matched literally, not as a whole word — see termMatcher() in check-vocab-gate.ts.

ADR 260804-021140 retired "integration", "connector", "adapter" and "provider" as USER-FACING nouns and settled on Connections as the umbrella. (Its two regions, Messaging and Accounts, were later folded into one list of apps by ADR 260927-033250; the retired nouns still stand.) The copy sweep shipped in DOR-1754 (UI audit batch 08); this wave is the guard that keeps it swept. Singular AND plural are listed because a term is fenced with a word boundary — banning "adapter" alone leaves "Adapters" on screen. What the ADR deliberately does NOT retire is the architecture: RelayAdapter, ConnectorProvider, /api/connectors/providers/*, the marketplace package types authors write, and the model-provider sense OpenCode uses. Those live in the scoped-word registry in the ADR's own table, and every one of them is allowlisted per file in allowlist.json with the domain reason — never exempted here, because the word is only correct in the places that table names. Identifiers, type names, package names and code comments are out of scope for a vocabulary sweep (AGENTS.md) and the gate never reads them.

What code calls a "community" is a "space" to the person reading (specs/dorkos-account-by-default, decision D6). The rename is user-facing only for now: identifiers, routes (/api/communities), CLI verbs (`dorkos community`), config keys, DB tables and the cloud wire contract keep the word until DOR-2639 renames them, and the gate never reads those positions. Singular and plural are listed because a term is fenced with a word boundary. Docs prose is scanned for this wave too (MDX_SCANNED_WAVES); a literal command or route that still says community belongs in inline code, which the docs scan blanks. Every surviving copy-position use is a scoped, reasoned allowlist entry — the open-source Community server's own pages, the marketplace's community-source sense, and the like.

The 2026-10 vision reset (meta/VISION.md, meta/VOICE.md) retired three positioning lines and one link for good. "Operating system for AI agents" in every spelling was the old category line; DorkOS is now "a workspace for people and agents" (the product name DorkOS stays). "One place for every agent" was the 2026-08 category line it replaced, retired with it. "Equal accounts" and "agents (are) equal" describe an internal design principle that public copy never states; a bare "equal to humans" is deliberately NOT a term, because it is an ordinary benchmark sentence and the claim always names agents. A Discord invite link points at a server DorkOS does not have. The bare word "Discord" is NOT banned: it is a real app people connect. Terms are phrases, matched with any run of whitespace between words (termMatcher), so a JSX line wrap does not hide one. This list is a SUBSET of scripts/check-banned-words.sh's regex for the same families: that regex accepts the qualifiers "AI", "autonomous" and "coding" in any order, while a term here is literal, so this lists the spellings people actually wrote. Both fence every phrase as whole words, so "Unequal accounts" and "your agents equally" never fire. This wave covers render-path strings in app source only. Docs MDX, blog posts, READMEs and the operating skills are guarded by check-banned-words.sh, which reports a hit once and honours this directory's allowlist.json for docs pages (the vocab-allow marker is banned there), so wave 6 stays out of MDX_SCANNED_WAVES on purpose (the same split as wave 2). An allowlist entry meant to exempt a docs line from wave 6 must name at least one term below. meta/VOICE.md is the single list of words DorkOS uses and never uses.
terms: operating system for autonomous AI agents
operating system for AI coding agents
one place for every AI agent
